rationale: While the case study addresses drinking water access in an informal settlement in Bogotá, Colombia (Criterion 1 and Criterion 4), the intervention/exposure examined is a community service-learning project focused on technological design and implementation of a rainwater harvesting and treatment system and healthy housing education. Lack of a formal aqueduct is mentioned solely as problem background; no legal, administrative, regulatory, tenure, tariff, discretion, enforcement, or institutional governance mechanism governing service access is analysed (E03).
plain_vs_narrow_note: Both the narrow rule-type reading and the literal/plain Criterion 2 wording yield exclude: although set in an informal settlement lacking a formal aqueduct, the study describes a university service-learning technological rainwater treatment and health education project implemented with an NGO rather than examining any legal, administrative, institutional, regulatory, or governance mechanism.
